chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the ornaments, 'Should I purify (pay Zakat)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Then there would not remain anything from it'.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحُلِيِّ: Ornaments, specifically jewelry worn for adornment
key_terms.يُزَكَّى: To be purified (referring to the payment of Zakat)

ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on gold jewelry and ornaments in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that personal ornaments (huliy) are exempt from Zakat, using the rhetorical device of hyperbole to emphasize their distinct status from trade goods or stored wealth. This ruling aligns with the Shia juristic consensus that Zakat applies primarily to specific categories of assets (such as gold, silver, and livestock) rather than all forms of property, distinguishing between consumption and accumulation. The response underscores the practical wisdom of the Imams in relieving believers of burdens on items used for personal adornment, which are not typically considered liquid capital.
